hint: The basic structural and functional unit of life.
easy_answer: A cell is the basic structural and functional unit of a living organism.

question_text: What is the function of nucleus?
hint: It contains genetic material and controls cell activities.
easy_answer: The nucleus contains genetic material and regulates many cellular activities.

question_text: What is the function of cell membrane?
hint: It controls movement of substances into and out of the cell.
easy_answer: The cell membrane selectively regulates movement of substances into and out of the cell.

hint: The jelly-like region where many cell activities occur.
easy_answer: Cytoplasm is the semifluid region between the cell membrane and nucleus where many metabolic reactions occur.

hint: A structure carrying genetic information.
easy_answer: A chromosome is a DNA-containing structure that carries genes.

hint: Formation of new cells from an existing cell.
easy_answer: Cell division is the process by which a cell divides to form new cells.

hint: A cell division producing genetically similar daughter cells.
easy_answer: Mitosis is a type of cell division that usually produces two genetically similar daughter cells.

hint: For growth, repair and replacement of cells.
easy_answer: Mitosis is important for growth, tissue repair and replacement of cells.

hint: Application of biological systems for useful purposes.
easy_answer: Biotechnology applies living organisms, cells or biological molecules to useful products and processes.

hint: Deliberate modification of genetic material using biotechnology.
easy_answer: Genetic engineering involves deliberate modification or transfer of genetic material using molecular techniques.

hint: DNA formed by joining DNA from different sources.
easy_answer: Recombinant DNA is DNA constructed by combining genetic material from different sources.

question_text: What is a genetically modified organism?
hint: An organism whose genetic material has been deliberately altered.
easy_answer: A genetically modified organism has genetic material deliberately changed using biotechnology.

hint: Growing cells or tissues under controlled conditions.
easy_answer: Tissue culture is the growth of cells, tissues or organs under controlled laboratory conditions.

hint: Production of genetically identical or nearly identical copies.
easy_answer: Cloning is the production of genetically identical or nearly identical copies of a cell or organism.

hint: A cell capable of self-renewal and differentiation into specialized cell types.
easy_answer: A stem cell can self-renew and can differentiate into one or more specialized cell types.

hint: Treatment by introducing, removing or modifying genetic material to address disease.
easy_answer: Gene therapy aims to treat disease by adding, removing or modifying genetic material in cells.

question_text: State one use of biotechnology in medicine.
hint: Production of medicines such as insulin.
easy_answer: Biotechnology is used to produce medicines and therapeutic products such as recombinant insulin.

question_text: State one use of tissue culture in plants.
hint: Rapid multiplication of disease-free plants.
easy_answer: Plant tissue culture can rapidly multiply plants and help produce disease-free planting material.

question_text: Why are enzymes useful in biotechnology?
hint: They catalyse specific biological reactions.
easy_answer: Enzymes are useful because they catalyse specific biochemical reactions efficiently.

question_text: State one benefit of biotechnology in agriculture.
hint: It can support improved crop varieties or useful bio-products.
easy_answer: Biotechnology can help develop improved crop traits, biofertilizers and other agricultural products.
